$comment: Fixes knext bundles for vinext ahead of upstream releases. `vinext` is the ONLY version these patches were validated against; `pristine` records the sha256 of each target file in that published tarball. Bumping the vinext pin without re-porting and re-validating every patch fails vinext-patches.test.ts.

patches.summary: Pages Router: a `/_next/data/...` request reaches getServerSideProps with the original data URL as `req.url` (Next.js parity), not the normalized page path.
Server builds: a `require()` of a CommonJS dependency resolves the package's `require` export condition even when Vite would externalize that package.
Nitro builds: a `turbopack.resolveExtensions` list without `.mjs` no longer hides Nitro's own preset entry (the build failed to resolve it).
Nitro builds: dependencies of the RSC environment are bundled, so a package's `react-server` export condition is honoured.
Web Worker bundles: `process.env.NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID` is inlined, as it is in the rest of the app.
Nitro builds: `outputFileTracingIncludes` / `outputFileTracingExcludes` from next.config are applied to the traced server dependencies.
`experimental.lightningCssFeatures.include`'s `custom-media-queries` entry now also turns on lightningcss's `drafts.customMedia` parser flag, so `@custom-media` can parse at all.

App Router: a GET/HEAD request for an unmatched path whose `Sec-Fetch-Dest` is a non-HTML subresource destination (image, font, script, ...) gets a plain-text 404 instead of the rendered not-found page.
Warn once, matching Next.js, when a route's resolved `runtime` is `edge`/`experimental-edge` — the Edge Runtime deprecation notice was never emitted.
A bare `//` (in any literal/percent-encoded form, with nothing after it) is no longer treated as an open-redirect shape, matching Next.js serving it as the index route.

next/image: the optimizer path honours `trailingSlash`, and a custom `loader` prop gets the built-in loader's per-breakpoint `srcSet` treatment (quality passed through as given, not forced to 75). The upstream PR also wires up `images.loaderFile`; that part is not bundled (see the patch header) and `loaderFile` remains ignored until the upstream release.

A server action's redirect, when invoked via fetch (the client-side router path), now always answers HTTP 200 like Next.js does — it previously fell back to 303 unless the action had already been forwarded, the target was an ancestor/stale-sibling route, or the target ran on a different runtime. The no-JS, progressive-enhancement form-POST redirect path is unchanged and still answers 303.
